summary: Led primary energy Reel in Boonchu's order: curiosity, second hook, setup, payoff, punch; scroll-, value- and laugh-tested

top.curiosity_screen: This sweat at dawn is about your afternoon slump.
top.curiosity_say: This sweat... is about your afternoon slump.
top.second_hook: You fight the afternoon with coffee. For me, the whole day starts here.
top.setup: Led primary. Five Surya A, five B, then asana after asana on my count.
top.payoff: The heat comes from inside, breath and movement together. For me, this is my energy for the day.
top.punch: My body makes this heat by itself. The coffee is for... my personality.
top.shots: 1 CURIOSITY: second phone flat at the front edge of one mat, slow motion, a sweat drop falling onto the mat during Chaturanga in Surya B (ask that student first). 2 SECOND HOOK: wide of the room in the 4th or 5th Surya B, everyone wet, moving together. 3 SETUP: you at the front counting the Surya B, then the room moving into the first standing asana. 4 PAYOFF: close on a back with sweat during a standing asana hold, ribs expanding with the breath; one shot of a wet towel or mat edge. 5 PUNCH: after class, towel on your shoulder, to camera, flat; pause before 'my personality', hold silence after.
notes: scroller 1: Linking dawn sweat to my slump opens a small gap. The second hook just repeats the coffee jab and ends on the teacher, not me.
practitioner 2: The payoff is generic, but the punch works: 'The coffee is for my personality' is dry, self-deprecating and calls back to the heat line. Best laugh in the set.

editor 2: The sweat/slump link is a strange enough opener to make people curious. Beat 4 just restates beat 2 instead of closing the loop. 'The coffee is for... my personality' is the strongest laugh in the set, self-deprecating with the surprise at the end.

top.curiosity_screen: You fight your afternoon slump at the wrong time.
top.curiosity_say: You fight your afternoon slump... at the wrong time.
top.second_hook: Afternoon, you can only borrow. Morning, you can build.
top.setup: Today I teach led primary. Whole room moves to my Sanskrit count.
top.payoff: One breath, one movement. Body heats from inside. For me, six days a week since 2008, this is the build.
top.punch: My morning? Alarm. Tea or coffee. Nauli. Shala. ... Hardest asana? Still the alarm.
top.shots: CURIOSITY: you to camera in the empty shala before anyone arrives, text on screen. SECOND HOOK: students arriving, mats unrolling, morning light from the door. SETUP: tripod wide at the back, the room in Surya Namaskara A on your count. PAYOFF: close details: sweat on a mat, steady breath in Utkatasana, the room lifting in Utpluthih at the end; caption '6 days a week since 2008'. PUNCH: you to camera after class, counting the four on your fingers flat (alarm, tea or coffee, nauli, shala), then 'Hardest asana? Still the alarm.' Hold one second, no smile. Say it only if the alarm is truly your hard part. Spoken total about 65 words.
notes: scroller 2: Best of the set. 'Wrong time' hits my real pain and opens a gap. 'Borrow vs build' is a line I'd screenshot. It's not quite sendable yet.

practitioner 1: 'This is the build' pays off the borrow/build hook well and the Nauli detail feels real. 'Hardest asana is the alarm' is the old 'hardest pose is getting to the mat' joke, so it's predictable.
editor 1: Beat 2 closes the 'wrong time' loop at once. The punch spends a four-item list getting to 'alarm', and naming the alarm in the list gives the ending away. The alarm joke is also an old one.

top.curiosity_screen: Your afternoon energy comes in a can. Mine doesn't.
top.curiosity_say: Your afternoon energy... comes in a can. Mine does not.
top.second_hook: Mine takes about ninety minutes. And the whole room drinks it together.
top.setup: Today, led primary. My Sanskrit count. One breath, one movement, everybody together.
top.payoff: Five Surya Namaskara A, five B. Body heats from inside. Students tell us they feel awake after. For me too.
top.punch: Me? I still drink coffee before class. From a cup. ... I have standards.
top.shots: CURIOSITY: you to camera, one empty hand held up as if holding a can (no real can, no brand on screen), text on screen. SECOND HOOK: wide of the full room just before the first Ekam. SETUP: tripod wide at the back; your real Sanskrit count over the room moving together. PAYOFF: Surya Namaskara B jump-backs in sync, then students leaving after class (faces only if they say yes); caption 'students tell us: awake after'. PUNCH: you with a plain cup, no logo, flat: 'From a cup.' Beat. 'I have standards.' Hold one second, then cut. Spoken total 67 words.
notes: scroller 1: 'Comes in a can' is a clear image but sounds a bit smug. The 'room drinks it together' metaphor confuses me, and 90 minutes feels like too much to ask.
practitioner 1: The payoff just repeats the setup facts (Surya A and B, heat) plus a testimonial, with no insight. 'From a cup. I have standards' calls back to the can, but the laugh is weak.

editor 2: The can/mine contrast opens a real loop. But beats 3 and 4 are swapped: the Surya A/B count sits in the payoff, and 'For me too' is a limp close. 'From a cup... I have standards' is a real deadpan laugh with the surprise at the end.

top.curiosity_screen: Five breaths, nobody moves. That stillness is for your afternoon.
top.curiosity_say: Five breaths, nobody moves. This is for your afternoon.
top.second_hook: Energy is not speed. For me, the whole day comes from this slow breath.
top.setup: Led primary. I count, mostly five breaths, then the whole room moves together.
top.payoff: Still body, long breath, heat from inside. Nothing to decide. Students tell us they feel awake after.
top.punch: Six days a week since 2008. Hardest five breaths? The ones before... coffee.
top.shots: 1 CURIOSITY: locked-off wide, whole room holding one asana (Utthita Trikonasana or Paschimottanasana), total stillness, only backs and bellies moving with the breath. 2 SECOND HOOK: very slow push in on the same hold. 3 SETUP: you counting the fifth breath, then the room moving on together on your next count. 4 PAYOFF: profile close on one student's ribs expanding during a hold (permission), then a quiet wide of the room still breathing. 5 PUNCH: you to camera after class, flat, pause before 'coffee', hold 1 s after.
notes: scroller 1: Stillness on screen loses a fast thumb, but the contradiction in 'nobody moves' is odd enough to notice. 'Energy is not speed' is decent.

practitioner 1: Marked down: it frames led primary as mostly stillness and 'still body' as the source of heat, but the heat comes from the vinyasa between holds. 'The ones before coffee' is a mild, expected twist.

editor 2: Best loop: stillness as fuel goes against expectation, and 'energy is not speed' builds on it. Beat 4 lands the stillness payoff but forgets 'afternoon', and the 'students tell us' line is filler. The punch callback ('five breaths before coffee') works but is gentle.

all.curiosity_screen: Your afternoon coffee is answering the wrong question.
all.curiosity_say: Your afternoon coffee... answers the wrong question.
all.second_hook: It asks, how to stay awake. Better question... how to wake up.
all.setup: Today, led primary. Whole room moves to my Sanskrit count.
all.payoff: One breath, one movement. Body heats from inside. For me, twenty years, this is how I wake up. Students tell us they feel awake after.
all.punch: Okay, I drink coffee too. ... I don't ask it big questions.
all.shots: CURIOSITY: before class, chest-up to camera at the shala door, your own cup in hand, text big on screen from the first frame. SECOND HOOK: put the cup down on the desk, walk into the room, back to camera. SETUP: phone on tripod at the back corner, wide, recording from the first Ekam of Surya Namaskara A; use your live count as the sound. PAYOFF: close on feet jumping back in Surya Namaskara B, then the whole room in Navasana; end on students rolling mats after class, filmed from behind (faces only if they say yes). PUNCH: after class, same spot, same cup. Flat face, no smile. Hold one second after 'questions', then cut. Spoken total 65 words.
notes: scroller 1: The 'wrong question' line is clever but abstract. The second hook is wordplay that sounds like a lecture. I slow down, then keep scrolling.

practitioner 1: The payoff is the stock 'one breath, one movement, heat from inside' plus a student testimonial, so nothing new for a 10-year practitioner. The 'big questions' callback ties back to the hook neatly but gets a smile, not a laugh.

editor 1: Beat 2 answers the 'wrong question' loop straight away, so beat 4 only repeats it. 'Students tell us...' is filler. The punch callback ('big questions') works but is mild. 'Twenty years' rounds up 2008 (18 years), which reads as inflation.

all.curiosity_screen: How many coffees today? I count something else.
all.curiosity_say: How many coffee today? Okay. I count something else.
all.second_hook: Today I count for the whole room. In Sanskrit. About ninety minutes.
all.setup: Led primary. Five Surya Namaskara A, five B. Ekam, dve, trini... everybody moves together.
all.payoff: One breath, one movement. Body heats from inside. For me, this is the energy for my day. Beginners welcome, we teach you from zero.
all.punch: And my coffee this morning? ... Ekam.
all.shots: CURIOSITY: tight on your cup on the shala desk, slow push in, text on screen, your voice over. SECOND HOOK: wide shot of the room filling up, mats going down. SETUP: tripod wide at the back for the first Surya Namaskara A; use the real 'Ekam, dve, trini' audio from class, not a re-record. PAYOFF: close on hands and breath in Adho Mukha Svanasana while you count five breaths; one shot of you helping a beginner (only with their yes) under 'we teach you from zero'. PUNCH: you to camera after class with the cup, lift one finger, say 'Ekam' flat, hold one second. If it was tea this morning, say 'my tea this morning'. Spoken total 65 words.
notes: scroller 1: 'How many coffees today?' hits me. Then the second hook is about the teacher counting in Sanskrit for 90 minutes, and I don't care about that.

practitioner 1: 'Ekam' as the coffee count is the cleverest callback in the set. Marked down because the payoff turns into a pitch, and 'beginners welcome, from zero' implies led primary is where beginners start, which is misleading.

editor 1: 'I count something else' is a good loop, but beat 2 gives the answer away immediately. Beat 4 ends on a sales line ('we teach you from zero'), which wastes the payoff slot. 'Ekam' is a clean surprise to end on, and the best word in the script.

all.curiosity_screen: Coffee every afternoon? Watch one Sanskrit word move this room.
all.curiosity_say: Coffee every afternoon? Watch one word move this room.
all.second_hook: Not music. One count. For me, it sets my energy for the day.
all.setup: Led primary. Ekam, inhale. Dve, exhale. The whole room moves on my count.
all.payoff: You don't decide. You follow. Breath and movement together, heat from inside. Students tell us they feel awake after.
all.punch: Sixteen years I practice Sanskrit names. Hardest word in the morning? Decaf.
all.shots: 1 CURIOSITY: close on your mouth saying 'Ekam', hard cut on the word to the wide of the whole room raising arms at once (record live audio, no music anywhere in this edit). 2 SECOND HOOK: wide, room moving only to your voice, 3 or 4 counts. 3 SETUP: alternate close mouth 'Dve' / wide room folding, matching each count to the movement. 4 PAYOFF: over your shoulder from behind you, looking at the room following; detail of feet stepping back together in Surya B. 5 PUNCH: after class, you to camera, deadpan, one beat of silence before 'Decaf', cut immediately after. Students from behind or with permission.
notes: scroller 1: 'One word moves this room' is a nice visual tease, but with the sound off I can't hear the word. The second hook goes flat as the teacher talks about his own day.

practitioner 1: 'You don't decide. You follow.' is the truest and most useful payoff here, and it's the real gift of led class. The punch is muddled ('practice Sanskrit names', 'Decaf' reads ambiguously) and says sixteen years, which contradicts since-2008 (18 years).

editor 1: The 'one word' loop is real and 'Decaf' calls back to it well. But beat 4 ('you follow') never comes back to coffee or the afternoon. 'Sixteen years I practice Sanskrit names' is clunky and contradicts 2008. The spoken line also drifts from the screen text.

all.curiosity_screen: After lunch you crash. After 90 minutes of asana?
all.curiosity_say: After lunch you crash. After ninety minutes of asana?
all.second_hook: You think tired, right? No no. Students tell us... awake.
all.setup: Today, led primary. Five Surya Namaskara A, five B. Five breaths in most asanas. Whole room, my count.
all.payoff: Breath and movement together. The body heats from inside. For me, twenty years, still the same.
all.punch: Okay, coffee is also hot. ... From the outside.
all.shots: CURIOSITY: you to camera before class against a plain wall, text on screen. SECOND HOOK: end of class, students walking out the door with backs to camera, then cut back to you for 'awake'. SETUP: tripod wide at the back, Surya Namaskara A, then the room holding five breaths; keep your count audible. PAYOFF: close on the breath moving in the belly and sweat during a hold, then the room in Navasana; caption 'heat from inside'. PUNCH: after class you hold your cup, look at it, then at camera, flat: 'Okay, coffee is also hot.' Beat. 'From the outside.' Hold one second, no smile. Spoken total 61 words.
notes: scroller 0: I don't know what 'asana' means, so I'm lost. The second hook gives the answer ('awake') straight away, and 'students tell us' is weak proof.

practitioner 1: The setup is accurate, but the payoff never answers the hook's crash-versus-awake question. 'Coffee is also hot, from the outside' is a tidy wordplay callback with only mild laugh value.

editor 1: Strong open, but beat 2 says 'awake' right away. Beat 4 ('still the same') doesn't close anything. The setup is overloaded with counts. The punch 'From the outside' is a decent inside/outside reversal, so it isn't wasted.

all.curiosity_screen: Tired after lunch? Why do they feel awake after this?
all.curiosity_say: Tired after lunch? Why do they feel awake after this?
all.second_hook: About ninety minutes of sweat. Students tell us: awake. For me, all day.
all.setup: Led primary. One breath, one movement, on my count.
all.payoff: Breath and movement heat the body from inside. For me, it builds energy, not spends it. We teach you from zero.
all.punch: Me? Coffee or tea first. Twenty years of Ashtanga, still a beginner at... mornings.
all.shots: 1 CURIOSITY: fast 2 s montage of the hardest sweaty moments (Surya B, Chaturanga), then the end of class: wide of students sitting up after rest, calm, wet (from behind or silhouetted against the window unless they agree). 2 SECOND HOOK: wide of the room mid-practice, everyone moving on one count. 3 SETUP: you at the front counting. 4 PAYOFF: one shot of a newer student at the back following the count with everyone (ask first), for the 'from zero' line. 5 PUNCH: you to camera after class, deadpan, pause before 'mornings', hold silence after.
notes: scroller 0: 'Tired after lunch?' reads like a supplement ad and the answer (exercise) is obvious. The second hook gives the answer straight away, so there's no gap left.

practitioner 1: The payoff edges toward a health claim ('builds energy, not spends it') and ends in a pitch ('we teach you from zero'). 'Still a beginner at mornings' is a pleasant callback but low laugh, and twenty years doesn't match since-2008.

editor 1: The question opens a loop, but beat 2 just repeats it ('awake'). 'Builds, not spends' is a decent close, but the beginner pitch wastes it. 'Beginner at mornings' is a weak laugh, and 'twenty years' inflates 2008.

all.curiosity_screen: Afternoon slump? Watch what this room does at dawn.
all.curiosity_say: Your afternoon slump... watch this room.
all.second_hook: No no, not for the morning. For your whole day.
all.setup: Led primary. I count in Sanskrit, everybody moves. One breath, one movement.
all.payoff: Breath and movement together heat the body from inside. For me, I feel it all day. Students tell us they feel awake after.
all.punch: Yes, coffee or tea before. That is how I forgive... the alarm.
all.shots: 1 CURIOSITY: tripod low in the back corner, wide, whole room standing in Samasthitih in dawn light, then the first Surya A inhale, every arm rising together. Text on screen from frame 1. 2 SECOND HOOK: same wide shot, room folds down together on the exhale, hold 2 s. 3 SETUP: medium shot of you at the front calling 'Ekam', mouth clearly visible, room moving behind or in a cut. 4 PAYOFF: side angle along one row in Surya B, backs rising and falling on the breath, sweat starting on shoulders. 5 PUNCH: after class, you to camera, empty mats behind, flat face, pause before 'the alarm', hold 1 s of silence after it. Film students from behind; anyone recognizable needs a yes first.
notes: scroller 1: 'Watch' plus a visual buys a pause. 'At dawn' loses a 3-coffee office worker. 'For your whole day' is generic.
practitioner 0: The payoff is the generic heat line plus the recycled testimonial. 'That is how I forgive the alarm' is unclear and doesn't land.

editor 0: 'Watch this room' is an order, not a loop, and the spoken line doesn't match the screen text. Beat 2 ('not for the morning') answers a question nobody asked. 'Forgive the alarm' gets no laugh.
